purpose: Editorial review ledger; never imported as approved production items

items.stem: There are three clubs, but I can join only one. I need to ___ which one I like best.

options.rationale: Describing does not select one club.
Selects one option from several.
Visiting is not deciding which to join.
Explaining does not select one.

blocking_risks: Only one and one club strongly cue selection; may be a low-difficulty anchor.

items.stem: It was £8 yesterday, but now it costs £10. So the ___ has gone up.

options.rationale: Size describes dimensions, not the amount charged.
Number does not specify the amount charged.
Value can refer to monetary worth and is potentially defensible.
Price is the amount charged for the item.

items.stem: We are having a school information evening on Thursday. We would like to ___ all parents to attend.

options.rationale: Remind presupposes a known obligation or earlier arrangement.
Inform someone to attend is not the standard construction.
Invite someone to attend is the natural request.
Advise someone to attend is also grammatically valid and pragmatically plausible.

blocking_risks: Potential second key D (advise), plus grammatical-elimination clue for inform. BLOCKED.

items.stem: I know you have already agreed to bring the books, but I wanted to ___ you before tomorrow.

options.rationale: Invitation is an initial request to participate.
A warning suggests risk rather than recall of an agreement.
Explain you is ungrammatical in this structure.
Brings an existing agreement back to mind.

blocking_risks: Distractor C fails grammatical parallelism. BLOCKED.

items.stem: The school shortened lunch breaks. One unexpected ___ was that fewer students attended lunchtime clubs.

options.rationale: An intention is an aim, not the resulting lower attendance.
A proposal is a suggested plan, not the result.
A requirement is an obligation, not the outcome.
A consequence is a result of an action.

blocking_risks: Three distractors are semantically distant; needs better matched alternatives.

items.stem: The equipment is not the best available, but it is ___ for the basic tasks we need to complete.

options.rationale: Means sufficient for the specified purpose.
Implies unusually high quality, not merely sufficient.
Means more than necessary, not sufficient.
Means inappropriate for the tasks.

blocking_risks: Distractors are weakly matched and may be eliminated by polarity.

items.stem: The researcher avoided calling the programme simply a success or a failure. Instead, she offered a ___ assessment that considered differences between student groups.

options.rationale: Decisive suggests a firm judgement, not careful distinctions.
Uniform implies sameness, at odds with group differences.
Recognises subtle differences and qualified interpretations.
Superficial lacks detailed consideration.

blocking_risks: Stem explicitly explains the target; possible low discrimination at C1.

items.stem: The extra reminders were meant to improve homework submission, but students began ignoring every notification. In the end, the policy proved ___.

options.rationale: Would mean the reminders worsened the problem, not established by stem.
Could fit because reminders no longer improve submission.
Not established by evidence.
Could be inferred but not explicitly supported.

blocking_risks: Key not entailed; ineffective is defensible. BLOCKED.
